chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from his father, from Abd Allah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from some of his teachers, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) ruled regarding a woman whose husband died while she was pregnant; she gave birth before four months and ten days had passed, and she married before those four months and ten days were completed. He said: I see that he should divorce her, then not propose to her until the end of the two periods has passed. If the woman's guardians wish, they may marry her off; if they wish, they may keep her, and return his dowry to him.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةُ أَشْهُرٍ وَعَشْرًا: Four months and ten days (standard iddah for non-pregnant widows)
key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْأَجَلَيْنِ: The two periods (referring to the early birth period and the full iddah period)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a pregnant widow who gives birth early and remarries before completing the four-month and ten-day waiting period?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ali (AS) in *Al-Istibsar* addresses the complex overlap of the waiting period for childbirth (*iddah al-wiladah*) and the waiting period for marriage (*iddah al-nikah*) when a pregnant widow remarries prematurely. The solution of a subsequent divorce ensures that the woman remains in a state of legal waiting until the full duration of four months and ten days is completed, thereby resolving the ambiguity of her marital status. This case highlights the practical application of Quranic injunctions in early Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing the protection of lineage and financial rights through precise temporal calculations.
